questions.prompt: If \(y=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_nx^n\), write \(y'\) as a power series.
questions.answer: Differentiate term by term. The derivative of \(a_nx^n\) is \(na_nx^{n-1}\), and the \(n=0\) term differentiates to zero. Therefore \(y'=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}na_nx^{n-1}\). Equivalently, with index shifted, \(y'=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+1)a_{n+1}x^n\).

questions.prompt: If \(y=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_nx^n\), write \(y''\) as a power series in powers of \(x^n\).
questions.answer: First differentiate once: \(y'=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}na_nx^{n-1}\). Differentiate again: \(y''=\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}n(n-1)a_nx^{n-2}\). To write this in powers of \(x^n\), replace \(n\) by \(n+2\), giving \(y''=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2}x^n\).

questions.prompt: Find the recurrence relation for a power series solution of \(y'-y=0\) about \(x=0\), using \(y=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_nx^n\).
questions.answer: Write \(y'=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+1)a_{n+1}x^n\) and \(y=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_nx^n\). Substituting into \(y'-y=0\) gives \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}[(n+1)a_{n+1}-a_n]x^n=0\). Equating coefficients gives \((n+1)a_{n+1}-a_n=0\). Therefore \(a_{n+1}=a_n/(n+1)\).

questions.prompt: Using the recurrence \(a_{n+1}=a_n/(n+1)\), express \(a_1\), \(a_2\), and \(a_3\) in terms of \(a_0\).
Find the first four non-zero terms of the power series solution to \(y'=y\) with \(y(0)=1\).
questions.answer: From \(y'=y\), the recurrence is \(a_{n+1}=a_n/(n+1)\). The initial condition gives \(a_0=y(0)=1\). Then \(a_1=1\), \(a_2=1/2\), and \(a_3=1/6\). Therefore the first four non-zero terms are \(1+x+x^2/2+x^3/6\).

questions.prompt: Find the recurrence relation for \(y''+y=0\), using \(y=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_nx^n\).
questions.answer: Use \(y''=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2}x^n\) and \(y=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_nx^n\). Substitution gives \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}[(n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2}+a_n]x^n=0\). Equating coefficients gives \((n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2}+a_n=0\). Hence \(a_{n+2}=-\frac{a_n}{(n+2)(n+1)}\).

questions.prompt: For \(y''+y=0\) with \(y(0)=1\) and \(y'(0)=0\), use the recurrence to find terms through \(x^4\).
For \(y''+y=0\), explain why one power series solution contains only even powers when \(a_1=0\).
questions.answer: The recurrence \(a_{n+2}=-a_n/[(n+2)(n+1)]\) connects coefficients two indices apart. Even coefficients depend on \(a_0\), while odd coefficients depend on \(a_1\). If \(a_1=0\), then \(a_3=0\), \(a_5=0\), and all later odd coefficients are zero. Therefore the resulting series contains only even powers of \(x\).

questions.prompt: Find the first three non-zero terms of the solution to \(y''-y=0\) with \(y(0)=0\), \(y'(0)=1\).
questions.answer: Substitution gives the recurrence \((n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2}-a_n=0\), so \(a_{n+2}=a_n/[(n+2)(n+1)]\). The initial conditions give \(a_0=0\) and \(a_1=1\). Then \(a_3=a_1/(3\cdot2)=1/6\) and \(a_5=a_3/(5\cdot4)=1/120\). Therefore the first three non-zero terms are \(x+x^3/6+x^5/120\).

questions.prompt: For the differential equation \(xy''+y'=0\), substitute \(y=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_nx^n\) and find the coefficient condition for powers \(x^n\) with \(n\ge0\).
questions.answer: First, \(y'=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+1)a_{n+1}x^n\). Also \(y''=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2}x^n\), so \(xy''=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}n(n+1)a_{n+1}x^n\) after reindexing. For \(n\ge1\), the coefficient of \(x^n\) is \(n(n+1)a_{n+1}+(n+1)a_{n+1}=(n+1)^2a_{n+1}\). The constant term gives \(a_1=0\). Thus the coefficient condition is \((n+1)^2a_{n+1}=0\) for \(n\ge0\).
